description: Whether a rep checking in is at the outlet, and whether that needs explaining. Positions are JSON numbers — unlike money, these are genuinely doubles on both sides, and a string would be a lie about the type the rule operates on. See ../README.md, and the note there about why distances are compared with a tolerance while verdicts are compared exactly.

assessment.name: across the street is still at the shop
assessment.why: The radius is 150m because consumer GPS is routinely tens of metres out in a street of tall buildings. A rule that only accepted the pin would flag honest reps standing inside the shop.

assessment.name: two kilometres away needs a sentence
assessment.why: BR-VIS-2 asks rather than refuses. `reasonRequired` is the strongest thing this rule ever says.

assessment.name: a device with no fix at a shop that has one still has to explain itself
assessment.why: The one case where nothing can be measured and a reason is still required — a phone reporting no position at a placed shop is exactly what a faked check-in looks like. Note `distanceMetres: null` alongside `reasonRequired: true`: the two are independent, and an implementation that tied them together would get this wrong.

assessment.name: an outlet nobody has placed asks nothing
assessment.why: The mirror image of the case above, and the reason they are not one branch. Making a rep justify a gap in master data would blame them for it.

assessment.name: neither side has a position
assessment.why: Both gaps at once resolves to the outlet's answer, not the device's — the outlet is checked first, so nobody is asked to explain a shop that was never placed.

assessment.name: a remote channel asks nothing, wherever the rep is
assessment.why: A phone call is legitimately not at the outlet. Demanding a reason would record an exception where nothing exceptional happened — and a flag that fires on ordinary work is one supervisors learn to ignore.

assessment.name: presence not expected reports no distance even when both positions are known
assessment.why: Deliberately `inside: false` and `distanceMetres: null` rather than the measured pair. The question was never asked, so there is no answer to record — an implementation that measured anyway would put a distance on visits where being 'outside' means nothing.

assessment.name: a radius of zero admits only the pin itself
assessment.why: Not a configuration anyone would choose, and the boundary the comparison is written against: `<=` makes the exact pin inside even here.

assessment.name: the equator and the meridian, which is where a sign error hides
assessment.why: Both coordinates zero on one side and a degree away on the other. An implementation that dropped a sign or swapped latitude for longitude still produces a plausible number everywhere else; here it does not.

assessment.name: across the antimeridian
assessment.why: 179.9E to 179.9W is a fifth of a degree apart, not 359.8. Haversine gets this right through the half-angle sine; a naive difference of longitudes does not, and this is the case that catches it.

assessment.name: the same point in both hemispheres is not the same point
assessment.why: 44.46N and 44.46S are ten thousand kilometres apart. A `Math.Abs` anywhere in the latitude arithmetic makes them the same shop.

assessment.name: the poles are one point however far apart their longitudes are
assessment.why: Longitude is meaningless at the pole. A formula that weighted it without the `cos(lat)` term would report a distance here.

assessment.name: antipodes, where the haversine comes closest to leaving the arcsine's domain
assessment.why: The largest distance this formula produces, and the case nearest the only domain error it can have. Rounding pushes the haversine to 1 + 2^-52 here — above 1, which is why both implementations clamp before `asin`. Measured, though: `sqrt` of that value rounds back to exactly 1 (ties-to-even), so across 6.5 million antipodal pairs the clamp never actually fires. It is kept as insurance for a future change to the expression, and this case does not pretend to exercise it — removing the clamp breaks no test, which is a fact about the arithmetic rather than a gap in the file.
